Hydrocarbons: Alkanes and Their Names: Organic chemistry is the chemistry of carbon compounds. Carbon forms four covalent bonds and long chains. Hydrocarbons contain only carbon and hydrogen. Alkanes are saturated with only single bonds and have the formula CnH2n+2: methane CH4, ethane C2H6, propane C3H8, butane C4H10, pentane C5H12, hexane C6H14, heptane C7H16, octane C8H18. Naming (IUPAC): find the longest chain, number the carbons from the end nearest a substituent, name the branches (methyl, ethyl) with their positions and use di-, tri- for repeated groups: 2-methylbutane. Cycloalkanes have the formula CnH2n. Alkanes are nonpolar, have low reactivity, burn in oxygen and undergo substitution with halogens in light. Boiling points rise with chain length.
Alkenes, Alkynes and Aromatic Compounds: Alkenes contain a carbon-carbon double bond and have the formula CnH2n (ethene C2H4, propene C3H6); alkynes contain a triple bond, CnH2n-2 (ethyne C2H2). They are unsaturated and more reactive than alkanes, undergoing addition reactions: ethene + H2 -> ethane (hydrogenation), ethene + Br2 -> 1,2-dibromoethane (bromine water is decolorized: the test for unsaturation), ethene + H2O -> ethanol, and ethene + HBr -> bromoethane. Alkenes can show cis-trans (geometric) isomerism because the double bond does not rotate. Benzene, C6H6, is an aromatic ring with delocalized electrons; it is very stable and prefers substitution (e.g. nitration, halogenation) instead of addition. The name is numbered so that the double bond has the lowest number: but-1-ene.
Functional Groups and Their Compounds: A functional group is an atom or group that determines the chemical properties of a molecule. The main groups: alcohols (-OH; ethanol C2H5OH), aldehydes (-CHO), ketones (C=O between two carbons, propanone), carboxylic acids (-COOH; ethanoic acid), esters (-COO-; ethyl ethanoate), amines (-NH2) and amides (-CONH2), halogenoalkanes (-Cl, -Br). Alcohols can be classified as primary, secondary or tertiary; primary alcohols oxidize to aldehydes and then to carboxylic acids, secondary alcohols to ketones, and tertiary alcohols do not oxidize easily. Alcohols have high boiling points due to hydrogen bonding. Carboxylic acids are weak acids. An ester is made by the reaction of an alcohol with a carboxylic acid (esterification) with an acid catalyst: CH3COOH + C2H5OH <-> CH3COOC2H5 + H2O.
Isomerism and Organic Reactions: Isomers have the same molecular formula but different structures. Structural isomers differ in how atoms are connected (chain, position and functional-group isomers): butane and 2-methylpropane are chain isomers, and ethanol and methoxymethane are functional-group isomers. Stereoisomers have the same connections but different arrangements in space: cis-trans isomers and optical isomers, which arise at a carbon bonded to four different groups (a chiral center) and are mirror images that rotate polarized light in opposite directions. Main reaction types: addition (alkenes), substitution (alkanes with halogens, benzene), elimination (an alcohol loses water to form an alkene, with concentrated H2SO4), oxidation (alcohols), hydrolysis (esters with water or base give an alcohol and an acid or its salt) and condensation. Saponification is the hydrolysis of an ester (fat) with NaOH to make soap.
Organic Synthesis and Analysis Methods: Organic synthesis plans routes from simple starting materials to a product through several steps, for example ethene -> ethanol -> ethanal -> ethanoic acid -> ethyl ethanoate. Yield = (actual / theoretical) x 100%, and the overall yield is the product of the yields of each step. Products are purified by distillation, recrystallization or chromatography. Structures are identified by spectroscopy: mass spectrometry gives the molar mass (molecular ion peak) and fragments; infrared (IR) spectroscopy shows functional groups by absorption (O-H broad at 3300 cm^-1, C=O strong near 1700 cm^-1); NMR spectroscopy shows the environments of hydrogen atoms (number of signals, integration, splitting). Elemental analysis gives the empirical formula. Combining the data gives the structure.
